clue.text: German boy to take a brief look

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for German
Lance is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young German lad is told to have a quick peek at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is a verb meaning to look quickly or briefly at something.

clue.text: Energy shown by top lass playing more than one upright

indicators.note: the letters are put into play, so they move about into a fresh order

parts.note: go is drive or energy, as in 'full of go'
these seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outstanding girl shows plenty of energy while playing sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' sounds like a moral person, but the plural upright here is a pair of posts on a sports pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalposts are the vertical posts of a goal, so the plural word covers more than one upright.

clue.text: He, tantalising it, possibly brings about an unexpectedly unpleasant ending

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might form something else if arranged differently

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man teasing someone with something ends up causing a nasty surprise at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a story or event with a nasty twist at the very end, like a scorpion's sting.

clue.text: Not entirely risky engaging Arab coach

indicators.note: engaging means taking something in and holding it, so one piece goes inside the other
not the entire word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: chancy is a synonym of risky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dangerous trip involving an Arab coach driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims a synonym of risky, and that shortened word then wraps round the Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned motor coach used for outings, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Fly flag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a kind of artificial fishing lure
second meaning: a long narrow banner or pennant

explanation.surface: Two words that look like a command to hoist or flutter a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is both a long fishing fly imitating small fish and a long narrow ribbon or pennant.

clue.text: Hybrid fruit — Italian chap's after tons

indicators.note: after places the name behind the abbreviation that follows it in the clue

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
Angelo is an Italian man's name

explanation.surface: An Italian man comes in after tons of crossbred fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit, a hybrid citrus.

clue.text: Girl full of sex appeal in musical

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: An alluring young woman appearing in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage musical about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Moderate having a wide general appeal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: avoiding extremes, especially in politics
second meaning: mainstream, aimed at popular taste

explanation.surface: Describes a centrist politician or product that pleases most people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for centrist views and for unadventurous mainstream taste.

clue.text: Studies marsh grasses, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the spelling differs from the sound

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses growing in marshes

explanation.surface: Someone examines wetland vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' looks like a noun but is the verb, as when a student reads law.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is British usage for studying it.

clue.text: Displayed in class — how educational

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Something shown in a lesson demonstrates how instructive it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Showed is the past tense of show, a synonym of displayed.

clue.text: A tsar upset Muslim ruler in Russian city

indicators.note: upset means knocked into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: these five letters are rearranged
a khan is a ruler in Central Asian and Muslim lands

explanation.surface: A Russian emperor annoys an Islamic ruler in some city of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a city on the Volga delta in southern Russia, also giving its name to a lambskin fur.

clue.text: Country to help new one suffering setback

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the word order is read from the end

parts.note: aid is help
N is the abbreviation for new
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nation helping a newcomer who has hit a bad patch.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country of South Asia.

clue.text: Used in Japan, gamekeeper's knife

indicators.note: used in suggests something is contained within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A blade carried by a Japanese gamekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The panga is not Japanese at all; that is the surface misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: A panga is a broad-bladed machete-like knife used in East Africa.

clue.text: The time to bring down the curtain, taking everything into consideration?

definitions.text: The time to bring down the curtain
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: the moment everything has been spoken and finished, like the end of a play
second meaning: the idiom for 'ultimately' or 'in the end'

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is whimsical: the curtain falls once the actors have spoken all their lines and the play is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ultimately, after weighing all factors, and literally describes the point when talking and acting have finished.

clue.text: See 13
Looks round ship for some cosmetics

indicators.note: round means placed on all sides of something, enclosing it

parts.note: to eye someone is to look at them, so eyes means looks
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone glances round a vessel searching for makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliners are cosmetic pencils or liquids for outlining the eyes, so a plural of makeup items.

clue.text: Compensate for cancelled series

definitions.note: defines OFFSET, the six-letter answer this clue gives across 16 and 18 together

parts.note: a cancelled event is no longer going ahead
a set is a series; its letters go into 18-across, the second half of this answer

explanation.surface: Making up for a television programme that was axed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue covers 16 and 18 as one word, OFFSET: cancelled gives OFF here and series gives SET at 18. The source failed to link the two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset something is to counterbalance it, which is to compensate for it.

clue.text: A fag? I felt trip could be

indicators.note: could be hints that a different arrangement of these letters is possible

parts.note: these nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smoker wonders whether the cigarette caused a stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag is British slang for a cigarette; the question mark admits that a filter tip is only one kind of fag.
explanation.definitionFit: A filter tip is a cigarette with a filter at the mouth end, an example of a fag.

clue.text: See 18

definitions.note: a misprinted cross-reference to 16, whose definition 'Compensate for' covers both lights

wordplay.note: points to 16-across's clue, where the word series means a collection or run

explanation.walkthrough: This light has no clue of its own; it is the second half of OFFSET from 16-across, where series gives these letters. The printed cross-reference 'See 18' should read 'See 16'.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the letters complete the word offset, meaning compensate for, defined in the clue at 16.

clue.text: Petit déjeuner or cornflakes at ten? A bit silly around noon

indicators.note: around means wrapped about something, holding it inside
silly means foolish and muddled, so the letters get scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as more anagram fodder
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Choosing between a French breakfast and cereal at ten, a little daft so close to midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters wrap round the single letter for noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit déjeuner is French for breakfast, and a light Continental-style breakfast of bread and coffee is its usual form.

clue.text: Falls once more, knocked over by artist

indicators.note: knocked over means tipped upside down, so this down word is read upwards

parts.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone falls down again after being bowled over by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as a verb but is a noun, the waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is the great waterfall on the US-Canada border, often just called Niagara.

clue.text: Entirely at home with Dorothy Gale's dog

parts.note: someone at home is in
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Wholly relaxed at home with the dog from The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is a Latin phrase meaning totally or as a whole.

clue.text: See 19
Simple when taken on board by writer

indicators.note: taken on board means carried within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: A writer grasps a straightforward idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary or plain, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Sudoku, mostly fiendish, getting credit

indicators.note: fiendish suggests something devilishly twisted, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Solving a fiendish sudoku almost entirely earns praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiendish is also a sudoku difficulty grade, which hides its role here.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise or prestige for an achievement, which is credit.

clue.text: Girl showing anger, one having spurned love

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: spurned means rejected, so that letter is thrown out

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A young woman is furious, having been rejected by her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, and girl is crossword shorthand for any such name.

clue.text: Put up with partnership

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, runs scored together by two batsmen

explanation.surface: Tolerating a business relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batters at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, and a stand in cricket is a batting partnership.

clue.text: Not more than a tot drunk with meths!

indicators.note: drunk means staggering and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Warns against drinking even a small measure mixed with methylated spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Meths is British shorthand for methylated spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: At the most is an idiom meaning no more than a stated amount.

clue.text: Salad dish we locals prepared

indicators.note: prepared as in made ready or mixed, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: these eight letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Residents describe a side dish they made themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage with mayonnaise or dressing.

clue.text: Exhausted, American editor ahead

parts.note: US is short for American
ED is the abbreviation for editor
a team that is ahead is up

explanation.surface: A weary American newspaper editor leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means consumed completely, and colloquially worn out or tired.
